chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah and a number of our companions, among whom were Abd al-A'la, Abu Ubaydah, and Abdullah ibn Bishr al-Khath'ami, heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying:
Indeed, I surely know what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and I know what is in Paradise, and I know what is in the Fire, and I know what has been and what will be.

He said: Then he paused for a little while, and he saw that this had weighed heavily upon those who had heard it from him, so he said: I came to know that from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says in it:

key_terms.السَّمَاوَاتِ: the heavens; the celestial realms whose contents the Imam states he knows
key_terms.النَّارِ: the Fire; the abode of punishment whose reality is included in this knowledge
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the earth; the terrestrial realm mentioned alongside the heavens
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise; the abode of reward whose reality is included in this knowledge
key_terms.تِبْيَانُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ: a clarification of everything; the Qur'anic phrase indicating comprehensive exposition
key_terms.كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: the Book of Allah; the source from which this knowledge is stated to be known
key_terms.مَا كَانَ: what has been; past events and realities
key_terms.مَا يَكُونُ: what will be; future events and realities

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the Imam's knowledge through the Book of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith presents the vast knowledge granted to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام regarding the heavens, the earth, Paradise, the Fire, and events past and future. It then grounds this knowledge in the Book of Allah, linking it to the Qur'anic statement that it contains a clarification of everything. In Shia theology, this supports the Imam's divinely granted knowledge through the Qur'an.
